# How the Owner of the LA Dodgers Built an Empire on Policyholder Money

First listed: 2026-10-14 | Evaluation cutoff: 2026-11-10

[Back to library](../README.md)

## Source versions

- [Substack: How the Owner of the LA Dodgers Built an Empire on Policyholder Money](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/how-the-owner-of-the-la-dodgers-built) - 2026-10-14

Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

Gober and Morgenson examine Walter-group affiliate reporting, state oversight, A-CAP proceedings, guaranty protection and mutual-insurer preferences. Eisman adopts the regulatory-failure and asset-sale concerns. Primary records confirm material affiliate reclassification and negative rating outlooks, but not a rating downgrade or a blanket breach of a universal affiliate cap. Official biography contradicts the claim of no insurance background. Several stronger allegations remain unverified, and the discussion must not collapse investigations, rehabilitation petitions and bankruptcy into the same event.

Material reporting failure is documented, but legal conclusions, specific financing paths and broad insolvency claims need further evidence. The episode has valuable questions about related parties and liability protection, alongside overstatements about regulatory background, rating actions and guaranty recovery mechanics.

### 007. The legal ceiling is the lesser of 10% of invested assets or 50% of surplus, while restated affiliates are about 400% of surplus and therefore far over the limit.

**Mixed** | Tom Gober | material factual premise | supporting

[Source at 7:41-8:16](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/how-the-owner-of-the-la-dodgers-built) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The cited statutory thresholds apply to specified subsidiary securities and allow approved exceptions; a blanket violation cannot be inferred from all affiliated assets. The 400% ratio remains unverified.

Assessment test: Match each asset category to statute and inspect permitted approvals and surplus calculation.

- [Delaware insurance investment law, section 1313](https://www.delcode.delaware.gov/title18/c013/index.html) (None): Section 1313 limits specified subsidiary investments to lesser of 10% admitted assets or 50% surplus, but permits higher holdings with approval. Not a blanket limit on every affiliated asset.

## Framework and tools

- Trace affiliated exposure through legal entities instead of accepting labels.
- Compare invested-asset percentages with surplus percentages without confusing denominators.
- Separate statutory accounting capital from economic risk and risk-adjusted capital.
- Distinguish ratings from outlooks, investigations from guilt, and rehabilitation from liquidation.
- Examine protection transfer in pension buyouts and present-value guaranty limits.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- Statutory annual statements and affiliate schedules
- Affiliated investments as percentage of assets and surplus
- 2014 complaint and settlement history
- State examiner staffing and tax revenue
- Reinsurance counterparty tracing
- Guaranty association assessment caps
- Permitted-practice accounting and captive structures
